sentences.text: 4. As per contents of FIR, incident is said to have taken place on 31.10.2019 when the appellant alongwith co-accused is said to have committed rape upon the informant.

5. It is submitted that appellant has been falsely implicated in allegations levelled against him which would be evident from the fact that medical examination of the informant was done on the date of alleged incident but the medical report does not corroborate allegations levelled pertaining to rape.
It is submitted that the informant also does not have any injury as per the medical report.
It is therefore submitted that appellant has been unnecessarily implicated on account of previous enmity.
It is also submitted that appellant's previous criminal history of three cases has already been explained while appellant is under custody since 06.03.2025.
6. Learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State has opposed the appeal but does not dispute the said facts.

7. Upon consideration of submissions advanced by learned counsel for parties, prima facie, subject to evidence being led in trial, at this stage it appears that allegations as levelled in the FIR do not appear to be supported in the medical report although medical examination was conducted on the same date.
Previous criminal history of appellant has been explained.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions of learned counsel for parties, without commenting upon merits, it appears that the learned court below has failed to appreciate the material available on record.
In view of the above, the order passed by the court below is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly appeal is allowed and the order dated12.03.2025 is set aside.

9. Let appellant (Hari Om) be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.

(iii) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
